title: wt removal result
description: The one document a wt removal prints in JSON mode, on success and on failure (nothing else goes to stdout). `items` is always present (`[]`, never null), one per item in the order wt acted on them; `dry_run` is always written (true: nothing was changed and every outcome says what a run would do; a failed dry run also says true). An item's `path` is ABSENT for a branch item and `ref` is ABSENT for a detached worktree; `saw` is the status the user saw when confirming; `worktree` and `branch` are the outcome enums (a branch or remote item's `worktree` is `not_requested` once acted on); `reason` is one sanitised line (at most 200 characters, so it may be cut); `warnings` and `losses` are always arrays of sanitised lines (`losses`: what the engine's fresh re-check said removing it would lose; [] when nothing, or when it was refused before a re-check existed). `branch_tip` is the FULL 40-hex commit id of a branch this run deleted or MAY have deleted: a present `branch_tip` means the ref MAY NO LONGER EXIST, whatever `branch` says. It is written when the branch was deleted (`deleted`); deleted, then put back because a worktree took it (`retained_checked_out`) or because the worktrees could not be re-checked (`retained_unknown`); deleted and not restored, or re-created by someone else (`retained_unknown`); when git reported the delete but the ref could not be re-read, or reads back again (re-created at another commit, or anomalously at the same one) (`retained_unknown`); when git's update-ref failed and the ref was gone afterwards (`retained_moved`) or could not be re-read (`retained_unknown`); and when wt failed internally after issuing the delete (`worktree: failed`, or `not_requested` for a branch item; `branch: retained_unknown`). Restore a local branch with `git branch <name> <branch_tip>`, where <name> is the ref without `refs/heads/`, while git keeps the commit; a name starting with `-` (which `git branch` refuses) is restored with the create-only `git update-ref refs/heads/<name> <branch_tip> ""` (the empty old value makes it fail if the branch exists again). It is absent in a dry run and for every branch the run did not touch. FAILURE: `error` with `items: []` means the run failed before acting (a nil error is reported as "unknown error"). A usage error prints the document with `error` and `items: []` and exits 1 when --json was parsed before the failure (an unknown flag after --json, no targets); a flag error that comes before --json prints no document, only a plain `wt: ...` line, and exits 1. PARTIAL REPORT: `error` beside a non-empty `items` means wt met values outside this contract while writing the result; every item is still listed, the offending field holds the reserved sentinel `invalid` (a malformed `branch_tip` is left out), `error.message` (one line of at most 200 characters) names the first off-contract items by index and value and states the count of the rest ("and N more off-contract values"), and the caller must treat the run as having made every change the listed items describe. Pinned to wt/internal/removal/json.go by wt/cmd/wt/remove_contract_test.go; an outcome or key added there must be added here and in the samples in the same change.

kind.description: `remote` is a branch on origin (`wt remove origin/<name> --remote`, or an origin row ticked in the list). For it `ref` is `refs/remotes/origin/<name>`, `path` is absent, `worktree` is `not_requested` once the item was acted on (or `refused` / `skipped_changed` when a gate stopped it, with `branch` `not_attempted`), and `branch` describes the ORIGIN branch: `deleted` means a fresh read of origin proved the ref gone, `retained_moved` that origin's tip differs from the one the user saw (or the branch is already gone), `retained_default` the default branch, `retained_unknown` that origin refused the delete or could not be read. A present `branch_tip` on a remote item means the origin ref MAY be gone; restore it with `git push origin <branch_tip>:refs/heads/<name>` (or GitHub's Restore branch button on the merged PR). `invalid` only in a partial report.

name.description: A raw identifier (a worktree's branch short name, or its directory's base name when detached; a branch's short name). Carried verbatim: JSON escapes only C0 controls, so C1 and bidi characters pass through; a consumer MUST escape it before printing to a terminal.

path.description: A raw identifier, carried verbatim; escape before printing to a terminal.

ref.description: A full refname (refs/heads/<name>; refs/remotes/origin/<name> for a remote item), carried verbatim; escape before printing to a terminal.

saw.description: `in_use` appears in preview or dry-run (plan) documents, and in a run document only for an item refused before anything was attempted (an in-use target named to `wt remove`: `worktree` is then `refused`, `branch` `not_attempted`); `invalid` only in a partial report.

branch_tip.description: Full 40-hex commit id; present means the ref may no longer exist (see the document description).
